turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung reassured O-lan that everything would be taken care of, that their son would be guided well and that she had no need to worry about him or the family. He insisted that he would see her wishes fulfilled and that her eldest son would have a good life.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan asked Wang Lung if he had ensured that their son would be taught the ways of respect and duty towards his wife and her family, and if he had reminded him of the importance of providing for his wife and children.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung assured O-lan that he would see to it that their son would be taught the ways of respect and duty, and that he would remind him of the importance of providing for his wife and her family, as she wished.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan asked Wang Lung if he had spoken to the maid about the importance of her role in the family, and if he had reminded her of the duties she owed to her husband and his ancestors.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son, feeling a mix of nervousness and devotion, told his mother that he understood the importance of respecting his wife and her family and would do his best to provide for them.

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: The maid told O-lan that she had understood her duties and would serve the family with all her heart, ensuring that she respected her husband and his ancestors.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan told Wang Lung and the others that she felt reassured by their words, but she asked Wang Lung to ensure that the arrangements for her son’s marriage were completed swiftly, for her peace of mind.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that he would personally oversee the arrangements for the eldest son’s marriage, ensuring that everything was done swiftly and in accordance with tradition to bring her peace of mind.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan insisted that Wang Lung and the others work diligently to prepare for the marriage, her voice firm yet weakened by illness, as she clutched Wang Lung’s hand.

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: The maid told O-lan that she would work diligently to ensure that all preparations for the marriage were completed with care and respect, in accordance with her mother-in-law’s wishes.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung assured O-lan that he would see to the marriage preparations himself, assuring her that her son would be well taken care of and married with all the dignity and tradition that she desired.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan insisted that Wang Lung and the others move quickly with the marriage preparations, her eyes reflecting both urgency and exhaustion.

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: The maid told O-lan that she would work tirelessly to ensure the marriage preparations were completed with the utmost care, respecting her mother-in-law’s wishes.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan insisted that the eldest son should be informed about the importance of his marriage not just for himself, but for the future stability of the family.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son nodded hesitantly, expressing his gratitude and understanding to his mother and father, acknowledging the importance of the marriage for the family’s future.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan insisted that the eldest son should take his responsibilities seriously, reminding him that the marriage was crucial for the family's stability and future prosperity.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son told O-lan and Wang Lung that he would do everything in his power to fulfill his responsibilities and ensure the marriage went ahead as planned, his voice trembling slightly with the weight of the situation.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung assured O-lan and the eldest son that he would arrange for the best possible marriage preparations, insisting that their family's future was secure and that O-lan's wishes would be honored.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan insisted that Wang Lung and the eldest son must not neglect the family's financial stability and prepare for a future without her, her voice filled with a mixture of urgency and resignation.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son told O-lan and Wang Lung that he understood the gravity of the situation and would work diligently to ensure the family's stability, his voice wavering as he pledged his loyalty and commitment.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that there was another thing before she could die.

opening.speaker: Wang Lung
opening.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that she could not speak of dying and please him.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that she must die, for she felt it in her vitals waiting, but she would not die before her eldest son came home and before he wed the good maid who was her daughter-in-law, and well she served her, holding the hot water basin steadily and knowing when to bathe her face when she sweated in pain. Now she wanted her son to come home, because she must die, and she wanted him to wed this maid first, so that she could die easily, knowing her grandson was stirred into life and a great grandson for the old one.

opening.speaker: Wang Lung
opening.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that she looked twice as well as they said and years away from death.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that she would see him wed and then she must die.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung to sit here and drink the wine and eat the rice of his marriage, for she would see it all and this would be his bed of marriage since she was soon to be finished with it and carried away.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan asked Wang Lung if everyone had wine and if the sweet rice dish in the middle of the feast was very hot and if they had put full measure of lard and sugar into it and the eight fruits.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told her eldest son that she was now content and that he should look to his father and grandfather for guidance. She also instructed her daughter to observe her husband and his ancestors, pointing out the foolish woman in the court as an example of what not to do. O-lan insisted that her children had no duty to anyone else beyond these teachings.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan asked Wang Lung how that one could feed him and care for him as she did. Beauty would not bear a man sons!
